messages:
Anya L.: Quick sync request — we need a single fallback compatibility matrix for routing decisions. Primary axes: tokenizer parity, context length, and tool-calling. I want a short list of rules we can bake into runtime + console UX.
Matt H.: Are we gating fallback by customer tier? Dedicated/enterprise customers should not be silently downranked to a tiny hosted variant.
Josef: +1. Proposal: enforce tier policy: enterprise/dedicated = no auto-fallback unless explicitly allowed in account; standard = allow fallback to compatible variants; free = aggressive fallback.
Sophie: Tokenizer is the sneakiest. Different tokenizers change prompt boundaries and can break tool args. I think tokenizer mismatch = incompatible unless we can show <1% token shift on our eval set.
Kai: We already run a tokenizer drift check. Suggestion: add a metric `tokenizer_token_additions_rate`. If >0.5% on canonical prompts mark incompatible.
Anya L.: Console/telemetry requirements: expose a per-variant "compatibility score" (0-100) and show badges for tokenizer/context/tool parity. UX should warn on rollouts when the fallback reduces compatibility.
DevEx: Mockup idea: per-route toggle `allow_tokenizer_incompatible_fallback` with a clear warning. Also per-account override for enterprise with audit log.
Matt H.: Context-length fallback: small variants can't hold long KV caches. Do we allow auto-truncate? That breaks any tool-calls relying on full context.
Josef: Auto-truncate only for plain completions. For chat/tool-calls mark as incompatible. We need a runtime check for `context_ge_required` vs `context_available`.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for `compat-matrix-v2` -> canary=10% (region=us-west).
Sophie: Tool-calling parity: if target variant lacks the function/tool schema, it is a hard fail for fallback. Add `tools_supported` boolean to the matrix.
Kai: Implementation sketch: runtime checks flags in order: 1) tools_supported, 2) tokenizer_compatible, 3) context_ge_required. If any check fails, skip fallback and try next candidate.
Anya L.: Edge-case: same tokenizer and tools but smaller context — maybe allow fallback with an explicit truncation strategy and a clear telemetry flag `truncated_for_fallback`. But disallow for stateful flows (tool sessions).
Matt H.: Quota/billing: if we fallback a dedicated customer to a cheaper hosted model, billing and SLA implications — product needs a policy. We should tag fallback events so billing can reconcile.
Josef: Telemetry fields to add to traces: `fallback_target_model`, `fallback_reason` (enum: tools_mismatch|tokenizer_mismatch|context_shortfall|quota_blocked), `fallback_latency_delta_ms`, `tokens_saved`. Add these to trace sampling.
DevEx: UX on Rollouts page: show a fallback-rate heatmap by region & tier, and a safety slider to disable fallback when mismatch_rate > X. Also surface recent fallback traces (links).
Sophie: I'll produce test vectors: 120 prompts covering plain completion, multi-turn chat, tool-calls with structured args, and long context (>32k tokens). We'll run matrix checks across 8 variant pairs and report tokenizer delta + tool-schema diffs.
Kai: Runtime action items: add the three-flag check, increment a metric `fallback_attempts_total` with `reason` tag, and emit an event for fallback decisions.
Anya L.: Action items recap: Sophie -> test vectors (ETA Thu EOD). Kai -> runtime checks + metrics (canary this week). Josef -> update fallback policy doc and billing notes. DevEx -> console mock + per-route toggle. Matt -> confirm enterprise opt-out enforcement and SLA wording.
Matt H.: One final decision: when multiple candidates are compatible, priority should be: same-seat (pinned) variant -> quantized/optimized same-arch variant -> region-preferred cheaper variant -> remote-hosted fallback. Agreed?
Josef: Agreed.
Anya L.: Thanks all. We'll review canary telemetry after infra-bot finishes canary.
